memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens had been closed, and the rain had stopped falling from the sky. The water receded steadily from the earth. At the end of the hundred and fifty days the water had gone down. - Gen 8:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The same God who had opened the springs of the deep now closes them. The floodgates that poured out judgement are shut by the very hand that opened them. And notice how the waters go down: "steadily," "the water had gone down." God's work of restoration was not sudden or chaotic but orderly and sure, receding day by day until the earth could be renewed.

There is comfort in that word "steadily." God's restoring work in our lives is often gradual rather than instant. He does not always dry up our floods overnight. More often He works patiently, steadily, drawing down the waters little by little until we can stand on solid ground again. What matters is not the speed but the certainty - the God who sends the waters down does not stop halfway.

This is the God who not only judges but restores. He is in the business of making things new - drying floods, healing wounds, rebuilding what sin has broken. The same power that once brought judgement He now turns toward renewal.

If you are in a season of slow recovery - from grief, from failure, from a long trial - take heart from these quiet verses. God's restoration may feel gradual, but it is steady and it is sure. The One who began to draw down your floodwaters will not leave the work undone. He who restores is faithful, and He is patiently bringing you back to solid ground.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you in a season of slow, steady recovery?
- Can you trust God to complete the restoration He has begun in you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Restoring God, thank You that You not only judge but make all things new. When my recovery feels slow, help me trust Your steady, sure work, until You bring me back to solid ground.
